title: Cathedral of the Immaculate Conception, Chanthaburi 2026 Guide | ThailandAddict
metaDesc: Visit the Cathedral of the Immaculate Conception in Chanthaburi, Thailand's largest Catholic church. Gothic riverside architecture, a Virgin Mary statue set with 200,000+ gems, stained glass, hours, dress code and photo spots.
keywords: Chanthaburi cathedral, Catholic church Chanthaburi, jewelled Virgin Mary, Gothic church Thailand, Cathedral of the Immaculate Conception Chanthaburi
intro: A Gothic Catholic church on the banks of the Chanthaburi River and the largest in Thailand. Twin spires rise high, and inside you'll find a Virgin Mary statue set with more than two hundred thousand gemstones, a timber ceiling shaped like a ship's hull, and stained-glass windows that catch the light all day. It's just a few minutes' walk across the bridge from the Chanthaboon riverside community.

blocks.html: If you come to Chanthaburi and skip this spot, you haven't really arrived yet. The Cathedral of the Immaculate Conception — locals just call it the 'Chanthaburi Catholic church' — is the largest Roman Catholic church in Thailand. It sits on the Chanthaburi River across from the Chanthaboon riverside community. The building runs about 60 metres long in true Gothic style, with twin spires you can spot from a distance, and entry is free.

It began with Vietnamese Catholics who migrated and settled along the river in the early Rattanakosin period. The first small chapel went up in 1711, and it was rebuilt and expanded over time until the current, fifth building. The foundation stone was laid in 1906 and the church was formally consecrated in 1909, making it well over a century old. The twin spires you see today were taken down during World War II and only restored in 2009, returning the church to its complete original look.

blocks.title: Good to know
blocks.html: The word 'cathedral' means a church that serves as the seat of the diocese's bishop. This is the only cathedral in eastern Thailand, which gives it a different standing from an ordinary church.

items.note: Out and back in a day

blocks.html: Plenty of people come for the exterior, but most walk away more impressed by the interior — it's full of detail and very quiet. Here's what to look out for, point by point.

items: The jewelled Virgin Mary — the most talked-about highlight. The statue is decorated with more than two hundred thousand gemstones, roughly twenty thousand carats in total, on a base cast in pure silver and set with gold and various gems. It turns Chanthaburi's famous gemstones into a genuine work of art.
Stained glass — Gothic stained-glass windows ring the church, telling the stories of various saints. In the late morning, sunlight pours through and casts the colours across the floor beautifully.
Ship-hull timber ceiling — the curved wooden ceiling frame resembles the hull of a ship; some compare it to Noah's Ark. It's old craftsmanship that's easy to get lost in.
Bronze bells and twin spires — there are three bronze bells and the twin spires that have become the church's signature.

blocks.html: The church is normally open to visitors during the day, with no entry fee. But because it's a working place of worship, you should avoid wandering around taking photos during Mass (Sundays usually have a morning service around 06:00–09:30 and an evening one around 16:00–17:30). If you want to look around at your own pace, late morning to early afternoon on a weekday is your best bet.

blocks.title: Dress code and etiquette
blocks.html: Dress modestly — skip spaghetti-strap tops or very short shorts. Keep your voice low, silence your phone, and if a service is underway, wait or watch quietly from the back.

blocks.text: Where people like to take photos

items.name: Riverside front of the church
items.blurb: Shoot the full building with its twin spires and fit both the church and the river into one frame. It looks great by day and when the lights come on at night.

items.name: Niramol Bridge over the river
items.blurb: The bridge linking the Chanthaboon riverside community to the church side. Shoot back across it and you'll catch the church framed in the background.

items.name: Inside along the stained glass
items.blurb: Stand in the middle of the aisle and shoot down the line of columns with stained glass on both sides. Late morning is when the light is best.

blocks.html: The nice thing about this spot is that it sits right next to a walkable sightseeing area. Cross the bridge to the other side and you're in the Chanthaboon riverside community — an old timber street lined with antique houses, coffee shops, food stalls and souvenir shops, easy to wander through. It makes for a perfectly paced half-day around here.

items: Chanthaboon riverside community — cross the bridge from the church and you're there in 2–3 minutes. Old wooden houses, cafés and local eats.
Chanthaburi gem market — a buzzing gem-trading market, busiest on weekends, not far from the church.
Local eats in the old quarter — Chanthaburi stir-fried noodles with crab, pork-stuffed noodle soup and local sweets, all found around the riverside area.

faq.q: Is there an entry fee for the Cathedral of the Immaculate Conception?
faq.a: Entry is free. But it's a working church still used for services, so dress modestly and keep quiet, especially during Mass.

faq.q: What is the jewelled Virgin Mary?
faq.a: It's a Virgin Mary statue inside the church decorated with more than two hundred thousand gemstones, roughly twenty thousand carats in total, on a base cast in pure silver and set with gold and various gems. It's the highlight most visitors come to see.

faq.q: What time does the church open, and when's best to go?
faq.a: It's open to visitors during the day. Late morning to early afternoon on a weekday is best, since there are fewer people and the light through the stained glass is lovely. On Sundays there's usually a morning Mass around 06:00–09:30 and an evening one around 16:00–17:30, which are best avoided so you don't disturb the service.

faq.q: Where can I go after visiting the cathedral?
faq.a: Cross the bridge to the other side and you're in the Chanthaboon riverside community, just 2–3 minutes' walk away, with old wooden houses, cafés, local food and souvenirs. It's perfect for a half-day around here.

faq.q: How old is this church, and what style is it?
faq.a: The current building was consecrated in 1909 and is well over a century old. It's Gothic architecture, about 60 metres long, with twin spires, a ship-hull timber ceiling and stained-glass windows.
